To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
microwave-assisted solvent extractable polycyclic aromatic compounds in tunnel dust were quantified accurately by isotope-diluted mass spectrometry using deuterium-labeled compounds.

the recovery yields of deuterium-labeled PAHs (PAHs-D) were lower in tunnel dust samples than in standard materials and that the observed concentrations of polycyclic aromatics hydrocarbons obtained by microwave-assisted solvent extract ion combined with isotope dilution mass spectrometric analysis were reasonable.
MAE combined with IDMS using D-PAH is applicable to the analysis of PAHs in tunnel dust, although the recovery yields of some heavy D-PAH (MW≥264) were <50% because of the high content of char.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of MAE to IDMS for the accurate quantification of PAHs in tunnel dust samples.
the use of MAE-IDMS for quantification of PAHs in tunnel dust, which is expected to be useful as a reference method for PAH analysis in environmental samples.
the use of MAE-IDMS with D-PAH standards to determine the concentration of PAHs in tunnel dust.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MAE with a mixture of methanol/toluened at 160°C and 40 min is the most effective extraction method for PAHs in tunnel dust, and MAE-IDMS is a reliable method for quantifying PAHs in the tunnel dust.
MAE-IDMS with deuterium-labelled 16 PAHs is a useful technique for quantifying extractable PAHs in environmental samples, even though recovery rates of D-PAHS are low.
MAE combined with IDMS using D-PAH is a powerful tool for quantification of PAHs in dust samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MAE-IDMS is useful for accurate quantification of PAHs in char-rich samples.
MAE with a solvent mixture of methanol/toluence (1:3) at 160 °C for 40 min combined with IDMS using D-PAH is useful for accurate quantification of PAHs in tunnel dust samples.

PAHs and their isotope-labelled analogues can be quantitatively extracted by MAE with methanol/toluane mixture from dust samples with a low char content, but that the recovery yields of the labelled PAHs decrease with increasing molecular weight.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MAE-IDMS can be applied to the accurate quantification of PAHs in dust samples with a large content of carbonaceous materials.
MAE-IDMS using D-PAH is a useful method for quantifying PAHs, especially for samples with a large amount of char, such as tunnel dust.
, although the use of D-PAHS is important to obtain accurate PAH concentrations in samples with high char contents by MAE-ID MS, it is necessary to confirm the recovery yields of each D-PAH.
